$comment: GET /rest/adAccounts/{adAccountId}/adCampaigns/{campaignID}, read from LinkedIn's August 2026 Campaign Management reference. A read is the honest first action: creating a campaign is not one self-contained operation -- it needs an existing Ad Account, organization, targeting decision, budget and bidding strategy, and often a campaign group before it can produce anything useful.
title: LinkedIn ad campaign
$idempotencyComment: This is a read-only GET, so replay does not create or alter an ad. LinkedIn documents no idempotency key for campaign creation; that omission matters when a write action is added, but inventing a key here would imply a guarantee the API does not make.

request.$pathComment: LinkedIn requires BOTH numeric ids in the path. The campaign id is not globally addressable through a shorter /adCampaigns/{id} route in the current account-scoped API.

config.label: Ad Account ID
config.description: The numeric Sponsored Account id from Campaign Manager; send digits only, without the urn:li:sponsoredAccount: prefix.

config.label: Campaign ID
config.description: The numeric campaign id within that Ad Account; send digits only, without a sponsoredCampaign URN prefix.

outputShape.description: The immutable sponsored-account URN that owns the campaign.
The user-managed campaign status, such as ACTIVE, PAUSED or DRAFT.
The placement family, such as SPONSORED_UPDATES or TEXT_AD.
True when the campaign belongs to LinkedIn's separate test Ad Account estate.
The daily budget amount. LinkedIn returns money amounts as decimal strings, not JSON numbers.
The ISO currency code for the daily budget.
Campaign start time as Unix epoch milliseconds.
Campaign end time as Unix epoch milliseconds, when one is set.

$outputComment: The GET response is the Campaign object directly at the body top level; the connector runtime exposes it under data. Money amounts remain strings because LinkedIn's schema and sample response use strings even though timestamps and ids are numbers.

contract.$comment: The path identifiers sent and Campaign fields read. LinkedIn publishes prose schema tables rather than a machine-readable specification, but declaring the contract keeps the action ready for drift projection if that changes.
